headline: August 20: EC announces presidential election schedule
summary: The Election Commission has set the date for the presidential election, with nomination papers to be submitted by August 13.
details: The Election Commission (EC) has announced that the presidential election will be held on August 20, with polling taking place from 2:00pm to 5:00pm.
EC Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed shared the schedule this afternoon at the commission's headquarters in Agargaon, Dhaka.
According to the announcement, nomination papers must be submitted on August 13 between 10:00am and 4:00pm.
The scrutiny of these nomination papers is scheduled to begin at 10:00am on August 16 and will continue until the process is completed.
The schedule was finalized following consultations between the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and the Speaker of parliament, in accordance with the Presidential Election Act, 1991.
The EC has already received the electoral roll, which consists of 350 members of parliament, from the Parliament Secretariat.
The commission has held a meeting to finalize preparations, and all remaining administrative procedures will be completed according to the timeline.
caption:
The date is set. Bangladesh will hold its presidential election on August 20.

The Election Commission (EC) has announced that the presidential election will be held on August 20, with polling taking place from 2:00pm to 5:00pm.

EC Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed shared the schedule this afternoon at the commission's headquarters in Agargaon, Dhaka.

According to the announcement, nomination papers must be submitted on August 13 between 10:00am and 4:00pm.

The scrutiny of these nomination papers is scheduled to begin at 10:00am on August 16 and will continue until the process is completed.

The schedule was finalized following consultations between the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and the Speaker of parliament, in accordance with the Presidential Election Act, 1991.

The EC has already received the electoral roll, which consists of 350 members of parliament, from the Parliament Secretariat.

The commission has held a meeting to finalize preparations, and all remaining administrative procedures will be completed according to the timeline.

headline: July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum opens to visitors
summary: The museum showcases artifacts from the student-led movement, with a 'red telephone' among the most popular exhibits.
details: The July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum has officially opened its doors to the general public, allowing visitors to explore the history of the recent student-led uprising.
The museum features a variety of artifacts and memorabilia from the movement, documenting the events and sacrifices of those involved in the the uprising.
Among the most striking exhibits, visitors have expressed a particular interest in the 'red telephone,' which has become a key attraction of the museum.
The museum aims to preserve the memory of the uprising and serve as a educational resource for future generations to understand the political shift in Bangladesh.
caption:
A new memorial museum dedicated to the July Mass Uprising is now open to the public.

The July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum has officially opened its doors to the general public, allowing visitors to explore the history of the recent student-led uprising.

The museum features a variety of artifacts and memorabilia from the movement, documenting the events and sacrifices of those involved in the the uprising.

Among the most striking exhibits, visitors have expressed a particular interest in the 'red telephone,' which has become a key attraction of the museum.

The museum aims to preserve the memory of the uprising and serve as a educational resource for future generations to understand the political shift in Bangladesh.
